dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt software (日医標準レセプトソフト), likely compiled with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL on Linux. Uses COPY-heavy structure with MCP (Message Control Program) table access pattern typical of JMA ORCA system.
evidence: EXEC SQL absent, EXEC CICS absent

purpose.domain_detail: JMA ORCA standard medical receipt (レセプト) software - inpatient history display/management screen (入院歴表示, ORCGI02). Handles patient admission/discharge records, ward/room information, disease name lists, and inpatient charge calculation.
purpose.summary: This program is part of the JMA ORCA medical receipt system and implements the inpatient history display screen (入院歴表示). It retrieves and displays patient admission records (PTNYUINRRK), ward/room information, disease names (PTBYOMEI), and other-hospital admission supplementary data (PTTAINFUKA). It handles screen initialization, data editing, and GUI widget state management via the MCP interface.

notable_features: Heavy use of COPY statements (28 copybooks) for JMA ORCA shared data structures
MCP-based table access (PERFORM 900-TBL-SELECT-SEC, 900-TBL-CLOSE-SEC) replacing EXEC SQL
EVALUATE MCP-STATUS ALSO MCP-EVENT for event-driven screen handling
LINKAGE SECTION with MCPAREA, SPAAREA, LINKAREA, SCRAREA for GUI integration
Japanese text in comments (EUC-JP encoded, rendered as latin-1 mojibake)
No COMP-3 usage despite numeric fields
Fixed-format source with max line length 74
verdict.notes: Source file is encoded in EUC-JP but decoded as latin-1, causing Japanese comments to appear as mojibake. The program is part of the well-known open-source JMA ORCA medical receipt system (circa 2002). The 'online-cics' program_type is used loosely - this is actually an event-driven GUI program using JMA's own MCP framework rather than CICS, but it is the closest enum match for an interactive screen-handling program.
